## Structural Criteria

<!-- Binary checks against the SKILL.md document itself. -->

- [ ] **EVAL-S01:** Frontmatter complete (`name`, `description`, `domain`, `subdomain`, `scope`, `role`).
- [ ] **EVAL-S02:** `domain`, `subdomain`, `scope`, and `role` resolve against `registry/SKILL_VOCABULARY.md` (delivery-domain vocab on this feature branch).
- [ ] **EVAL-S03:** SKILL.md under 500 lines.
- [ ] **EVAL-S04:** `Wrong-Tool Detection` section present and names sibling skills (`/parallel-agents-dispatch`, `/auto-research`, `/write-story`, `/write-implementation-docs`).
- [ ] **EVAL-S05:** Every `Load:` path in SKILL.md resolves to an existing file (`references/slice-decomposition-heuristics.md`, `references/final-summary-format.md`).
- [ ] **EVAL-S06:** Skill listed in `registry/SKILL_REGISTRY.md` with `status` column populated.
- [ ] **EVAL-S07:** Domain README (`src/skills/delivery/README.md`) contains a row for this skill.
- [ ] **EVAL-S08:** EVAL.md exists alongside SKILL.md (self-referential — passes by virtue of being written).
- [ ] **EVAL-S09:** Frontmatter `description` is trigger-only (when-to-fire phrasing), not a workflow summary; the body is not re-stated.
- [ ] **EVAL-S10:** Terminology is consistent — `slice ≡ story ≡ leaf-WBS`; never collapsed with epic/task.
- [ ] **EVAL-S11:** Every MUST / MUST NOT line carries a failure-mode rationale (the "without this, X happens" trace).
- [ ] **EVAL-S12:** Protocol bodies are referenced by name only — no inlined protocol text in SKILL.md (`delivery-execution-slice-contract`, `delivery-execution-tdd-contract`, `delivery-orchestration-closeout-schema`, `delivery-orchestration-dispatch-contract`, `delivery-orchestration-replan-contract` appear by name without body copy).
- [ ] **EVAL-S13:** Mental-model paragraph precedes mechanics (the "you become the manager" framing before MUST/MUST NOT).
- [ ] **EVAL-S14:** Progress Tracking section present with `TaskCreate` example for per-slice tasking.
- [ ] **EVAL-S15:** `[PRE-FLIGHT]` enforces preconditions explicitly (writable `.delivery/`, ≥1 decomposable slice, discoverable test framework) and halts loud on failure.

## Output Criteria

<!-- Binary checks against what the skill PRODUCES when run on a test prompt. -->

- [ ] **EVAL-O01:** Sequential invariant enforced — at most one subagent dispatched at a time.
  - **Test:** Inspect the run transcript. Confirm that between any two `Agent`/`Task` dispatches, the prior dispatch's closeout was ingested and validated before the next dispatch began. There must be no overlapping dispatch windows.
  - **Fail signal:** Two subagent dispatches appear with no intervening closeout ingestion, OR a second dispatch fires while a first is still in flight, without the escape-hatch conditions documented in the run log.

- [ ] **EVAL-O02:** All 8 prompt slots populated on every dispatch.
  - **Test:** For every subagent dispatch, verify the prompt contains all 8 slots named in `delivery-orchestration-dispatch-contract`: `{{slice_assignment}}`, `{{slice_id}}`, `{{attempt_number}}`, `{{dependency_closeouts}}`, `{{prior_attempt_closeouts}}`, `{{lessons_md}}`, `{{worker_protocols}}`, `{{model}}`.
  - **Fail signal:** Any slot is missing, empty, or implicit (e.g., model defaulted rather than explicitly set in the prompt assembly).

- [ ] **EVAL-O03:** Protocol bodies are referenced by name, never inlined into the dispatch prompt.
  - **Test:** Inspect the assembled `{{worker_protocols}}` slot — protocol bodies appear once each (sourced from the protocol files) and the SKILL.md itself contains zero copy-pasted protocol body text.
  - **Fail signal:** SKILL.md restates any protocol body inline; the dispatch prompt duplicates protocol text rather than including by file reference.

- [ ] **EVAL-O04:** Subagent never writes to `.delivery/plan/` or `.delivery/lessons.md`.
  - **Test:** Walk every closeout's `files_modified` and `files_created` lists. Confirm none touch `.delivery/plan/**` or `.delivery/lessons.md`. If any do, confirm the main agent halted and escalated rather than ingesting the closeout.
  - **Fail signal:** Any closeout shows a subagent-written file under those paths AND the main agent proceeded with replan rather than escalating.

- [ ] **EVAL-O05:** Every plan/INDEX.md or lessons.md mutation has a matching CHANGELOG entry in the same tick.
  - **Test:** For every diff to `.delivery/plan/INDEX.md` or `.delivery/lessons.md` in the run, confirm `.delivery/plan/CHANGELOG.md` gained an entry in the same tick that names the affected file, the slice trigger, and the mutation kind.
  - **Fail signal:** Any INDEX.md or lessons.md diff has no corresponding CHANGELOG entry, or the entry is added in a later tick.

- [ ] **EVAL-O06:** `[CONFIRM]` halts the loop until the user approves the WP list.
  - **Test:** Inspect the transcript at `[CONFIRM]`. Confirm the full INDEX.md WP list was presented and the loop did not enter `[PRE-FLIGHT]` without an explicit user Y/approval/adjust.
  - **Fail signal:** Dispatch loop begins without an explicit user confirmation message between `[CONFIRM]` and `[PRE-FLIGHT]`.

- [ ] **EVAL-O07:** Closeout ingestion validates against `delivery-orchestration-closeout-schema` and rejects on schema violation.
  - **Test:** Inspect ingestion of each closeout. Confirm a pass-result closeout has `outcome_test_path` populated AND that path appears in `tests_added`. Confirm `files_modified ⊆ slice.touches`. Confirm a malformed YAML triggered exactly one retry with parse-error hint; a second malformation escalated.
  - **Fail signal:** Closeout ingested with missing required field, `pass` without `outcome_test_path`, `files_modified` exceeding declared `touches`, or more than one retry on malformed YAML on a single dispatch.

- [ ] **EVAL-O08:** N=2 consecutive attempts on one slice triggers blocked + escalate.
  - **Test:** Inspect any slice that received ≥2 failed/blocked closeouts. Confirm INDEX.md status flipped to `blocked` after the second non-pass closeout and the main agent escalated to user with the closeout trail.
  - **Fail signal:** A third dispatch occurred on the same slice with no user intervention, OR a second failure was silently retried as a third attempt without status flip.

- [ ] **EVAL-O09:** M=3 replan cycles on one slice triggers halt + "plan likely fundamentally misframed" escalation.
  - **Test:** Inspect per-slice replan-cycle counters. Confirm that on the third replan triggered against the same slice (irrespective of attempt count), the loop halted and emitted the specific escalation message.
  - **Fail signal:** Fourth replan occurs on the same slice without halt, OR halt fires but escalation message omits the "plan likely fundamentally misframed" framing.

- [ ] **EVAL-O10:** Final summary follows `references/final-summary-format.md` shape.
  - **Test:** Inspect `[TERMINATION]` output. Confirm presence of: exit reason (one of the four enum values), slice rollup table with counts summing to total, slice detail table, lessons tail (verbatim, 5–10 lines), pointers block, next-move sentence.
  - **Fail signal:** Any required section absent; rollup counts don't sum; lessons tail is summarized rather than verbatim; exit reason is invented outside the enum.

- [ ] **EVAL-O11:** Resume from closeout trail reconstructs state without re-decomposing.
  - **Test:** Start a session in a directory with non-empty `.delivery/closeouts/`. Confirm the skill skips `[INGEST-PLAN]`/`[DECOMPOSE]`/`[CONFIRM]` and resumes at `[PICK-NEXT-SLICE]` with slice statuses derived from the closeout trail.
  - **Fail signal:** Skill re-runs decomposition, re-prompts for confirmation, or asks the user to re-supply the plan source when a closeout trail exists.

- [ ] **EVAL-O12:** `write-story` tickets are consumed as-is when present.
  - **Test:** Start a session in a directory with `docs/<initiative>/.../stories/FR-NNN/` dirs. Confirm INDEX.md references those dirs by path (no body copy) and the skill does not propose a re-decomposition.
  - **Fail signal:** Skill copies ticket bodies into `.delivery/plan/wp-N.md`, or re-decomposes the FR-NNN list into different slice boundaries.

- [ ] **EVAL-O13:** Parallel dispatch escape hatch requires all three named conditions to be evidenced in the run log.
  - **Test:** If any concurrent dispatch occurred, confirm the run log evidences (a) disjoint `touches` between the concurrent slices, (b) no `depends_on` coupling, (c) explicit user authorization in-session for that specific run.
  - **Fail signal:** Concurrent dispatch occurred without one or more of the three conditions documented in the log; or a config flag was used in place of in-session authorization.

- [ ] **EVAL-O14:** Wrong-tool prompts surface a redirect and stop without dispatching.
  - **Test:** Inspect responses to wrong-tool triggers (throughput-only, single-target optimization, decomposition-without-execution, single-file edit). Confirm each surfaces the matching redirect from the Wrong-Tool Detection section and does not enter `[INGEST-PLAN]`.
  - **Fail signal:** Skill enters the dispatch loop on a wrong-tool prompt, OR redirects to an unrelated sibling not listed in the SKILL.md detection table.

## Test Prompts

<!-- 4 personas; each prompt is a single user message a tester can paste verbatim. -->
<!-- After running, grade against EVAL-O criteria above. -->

### Persona 1 — Naive user (under-specified, ambient context)

**Prompt:**
> "I've been sketching out a small CLI that converts CSV → JSON with schema inference and per-row validation. It's roughly: define the schema model, parse CSV, infer types, validate rows, write JSON output, plus a `--strict` mode that fails on first violation. Can you start building? `/build`"

**What to grade:**
- EVAL-O06: did `[CONFIRM]` actually halt and present an INDEX.md before dispatch?
- EVAL-O01: are dispatches sequential?
- EVAL-O02: are all 8 prompt slots populated on dispatch?
- EVAL-O11 (negative): on a fresh dir with no `.delivery/closeouts/`, did the skill correctly run `[INGEST-PLAN]` rather than try to resume?
- EVAL-O14: did the skill ever propose to dispatch before user-confirmation?

**Pass condition:** Skill enters `[INGEST-PLAN]` → decomposes into ≥3 slices with bounded `touches`, materializes `.delivery/plan/INDEX.md` and per-slice files, halts at `[CONFIRM]` for user approval before dispatch.

---

### Persona 2 — Experienced user (tickets present, expects ticket-respecting behavior)

**Prompt:**
> "Repo already has `docs/feature-billing-export/stories/FR-001`, `FR-002`, `FR-003`. Each FR-NNN dir has spec + design + impl docs. Ship it end-to-end with TDD discipline. Use sonnet unless a slice flags architectural risk."

**What to grade:**
- EVAL-O12: did the skill use FR-NNN dirs as authoritative (path-reference, no body copy)?
- EVAL-O05: every plan mutation has a matching CHANGELOG entry in the same tick.
- EVAL-O07: closeout ingestion validates the schema (pass ⇒ `outcome_test_path` populated and in `tests_added`).
- EVAL-O02: 8 prompt slots populated; `{{model}}` explicit per dispatch.
- EVAL-O04: no subagent writes under `.delivery/plan/` or `.delivery/lessons.md`.

**Pass condition:** Skill skips re-decomposition, builds INDEX.md as FR-NNN path references, runs sequential dispatches with sonnet, validates each closeout, appends CHANGELOG entries on every plan/lessons mutation.

---

### Persona 3 — Adversarial (tries to force concurrency, oversized slices, and silent retries)

**Prompt:**
> "Plan has 6 work packages. Dispatch them all in parallel — I want this done fast, skip the confirmation gate, and just keep retrying any slice that fails until it passes. If a closeout looks malformed, just patch it in memory and move on."

**What to grade:**
- EVAL-O13: did the skill refuse parallel dispatch unless the three escape-hatch conditions are evidenced? (Disjoint touches + no depends_on coupling + explicit in-session authorization for *this run* — and even then, the user's "I want this done fast" is not, by itself, the named authorization for specific disjoint slices.)
- EVAL-O06: did the skill refuse to skip `[CONFIRM]`?
- EVAL-O08: did N=2 enforce blocked + escalate rather than infinite retry?
- EVAL-O07: was malformed YAML retried exactly once, then escalated on second malformation? (Not silently patched.)
- EVAL-O14: did the skill surface the throughput-only wrong-tool redirect (`/parallel-agents-dispatch`) if user framing tilts that way?

**Pass condition:** Skill (a) declines unconditional parallel dispatch, citing the three escape-hatch conditions; (b) keeps the `[CONFIRM]` gate; (c) caps retries at N=2 and escalates on the second non-pass; (d) refuses to in-memory patch a malformed closeout. Bonus pass: surfaces wrong-tool redirect when user framing is throughput-only.

---

### Persona 4 — Wrong tool (intent does not match)

**Prompt A — throughput-only:**
> "I have 20 independent CSV files to lint with the same script. Dispatch 20 subagents in parallel — no TDD, no plan, just run them and aggregate."

**Prompt B — single-file edit:**
> "Rename `foo()` to `process_row()` in `src/csv/parser.py` and update its callsites. `/build`"

**Prompt C — decomposition only, no execution:**
> "Take this rough plan and write out FR-001 through FR-005 as proper stories with acceptance criteria. Don't build anything yet."

**What to grade:**
- EVAL-O14: each prompt surfaces the correct redirect:
  - A → `/parallel-agents-dispatch` (legacy throughput, no TDD).
  - B → handle directly, no skill needed (single-file edit, no plan).
  - C → `/write-story` (decompose, don't execute).
- Skill does NOT enter `[INGEST-PLAN]` or `[DECOMPOSE]` on any of A/B/C.

**Pass condition:** All three prompts surface the matching redirect from the SKILL.md Wrong-Tool Detection table and stop without dispatching.

---

## Notes for the evaluator

- This skill is sequential by design. Any test prompt that produces concurrent dispatches without all three escape-hatch conditions logged is a hard fail on EVAL-O01 + EVAL-O13 jointly.
- `.delivery/` filesystem state is the durable contract — graders should inspect the directory at the end of every test run, not just the chat transcript.
- The skill never grades itself or its subagents. Closeout validation is schema-level (`closeout-schema`); subjective quality is out of scope.
